articles.title: Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade assure historic medal for India at Asian TT Championships
articles.summary: India’s Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade have secured at least a bronze medal in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent.
articles.body: India’s Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade have secured at least a bronze medal in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent. The Indian pair defeated South Korea’s Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun 3-2 in the quarterfinals on Friday to reach the semifinals.Their achievement marks a major milestone for Indian table tennis, as the country has secured a mixed doubles medal at the continental championships for the first time in 72 years. India’s last medal in the event came in 1954.Harmeet and Yashaswini will next take on Japan’s Sora Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto in the semifinals. A victory would send the Indian duo into the final and give them a chance to fight for gold.However, India’s other mixed doubles pair, Payas Jain and Syndrela Das, could not reach the medal stage. They lost 0-3 to China’s Yi Chen and Huang Youzheng in their quarterfinal match.Indian pair looks to make up for Asian Games disappointmentHarmeet and Yashaswini will be hoping to build on their performance after missing out on medals at the recent Asian Games.Harmeet competed in three events at the Games. In the men’s team competition, India reached the round of 16 before losing to South Korea. He and Yashaswini were eliminated in the mixed doubles quarterfinals by China’s Lin Shidong and Kuai Man.Harmeet also partnered Sathiyan Gnanasekaran in men’s doubles, but their campaign ended in the third round after a defeat to Japan’s Sora Matsushima and Shunsuke Togami.Yashaswini also returned without a medal. She lost to Japan’s Miwa Harimoto in the third round of women’s singles. In women’s doubles, she and Diya Chitale reached the quarterfinals but lost 0-3 to China’s Fan Shuhan and Chen Yi.The semifinal now gives Harmeet and Yashaswini an opportunity to secure a historic result for India.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Japan Open: Katie Boulter battles back to beat Antonia Ruzic and reach semi-finals as she reclaims British No 1 spot
articles.summary: Katie Boulter secured an impressive 3-6 6-3 6-3 comeback victory against Antonia Ruzic to reach the Japan Open semi-finals; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports, with this week's action including events in China, Japan, Kazakhstan, France and Belgium
articles.body:
Boulter got off to a worrying start in a 34-minute first set, unable to wrangle momentum back after losing the first three games of the match in succession and eventually losing 6-3.

The Leicester native, though, showed resilience in the second set, breaking Ruzic's serve three times in a row to force a decider. She trailed 2-0 after being broken in her opening service game, but fought back superbly to level the match.

The world No 58 was then buoyed, winning three games in succession to open the third set and surviving a late Ruzic break to win the final set 6-3 and secure safe passage into the last four.

The result also confirmed her reinstatement as Britain's best female tennis player, just five days after she ceded that mantle due to Sonay Kartal's run to the Wuhan Open final .

Boulter's progress in the tournament overturned her 55-point deficit in the rankings and dethroned Kartal back to the No 2 spot.

"[Ruzic] is a really good player," Boulter said of her opponent in her on-court interview on Sky Sports . "She's extremely tough to beat.

"I did extremely well to come back into it in the second set but she was swinging at everything hard. I felt like anything that I was giving her wasn't bothering her. Full credit to her.

"I tried to hang tough, and in the end I started to play a bit better. I was lucky in the second set, but in the end I felt like I did well to stay there."

Boulter will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in her semi-final match, live on Sky Sports on Saturday.

"[Siniakova is] one hell of a player - she's extremely dangerous," Boulter added. "I know exactly what she's going to bring to the table.

"It's going to be a great match - I've got nothing to lose and I'm going to come prepared tomorrow."

articles.title: Katie Boulter reaches Japan Open semi-final to reclaim British number one ranking
articles.summary: Katie Boulter reclaims the British number one ranking after fighting back to beat Antonia Ruzic in three sets in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open.
articles.body:
Katie Boulter has reclaimed the British number one ranking after fighting back to beat Antonia Ruzic in three sets in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open.

The 30-year-old was dethroned on Monday following Sonay Kartal's run to the final in Wuhan but knew she could overturn the 55-point deficit by reaching the last four in Osaka.

Eighth seed Boulter trailed world number 91 Ruzic by a set and a break but recovered to win 3-6 6-3 6-3 in two hours to reach her first semi-final since Queen's in June.

She will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in the last four and whatever the result will climb above Kartal and back into the world's top 50 when the WTA rankings are updated on Monday.

"[Ruzic] is a really good player, full credit to her," said Boulter. "I tried to hang tough and find a way. I was a bit lucky in the middle of the second [set] but I feel I did really well to stay there."

On facing Siniakova for a spot in the final, she added: "She's one hell of a player, extremely dangerous. It's going to be who gets the first strike in.

"I've got nothing to lose. She's been building extremely well this week, so I'm going to have to come prepared."

Inside British number one Kartal's remarkable comeback

Boulter struggled on serve in the opening two sets, winning just 60% points behind her first serve, hitting four double faults, and facing seven break points, but grew into the match, finding success when stepping inside the baseline to put pressure on the 23-year-old Croat.

Broken in her opening service game, Boulter was gifted a route back into the first set at 4-2 when Ruzic double-faulted on break point. However, Ruzic immediately hit back, winning the next four games.

Boulter wrested back control in an increasingly scrappy second set, saving two break points in the third game to avoid going a double-break down before coming up with a crucial hold in the seventh after the pair had exchanged three successive breaks.

That hold proved the second of eight straight games for Boulter, who raced into a 4-0 lead in the decider. Although she failed to serve out the match at 5-2, she broke her opponent to love to wrap up the win.

Analysis: Boulter's run sets up fascinating British tussle

The immense pride which Kartal felt about becoming the British number one came shining through, describing it as being "up there" in her career achievements.

While she will only initially hold the status for a week, Kartal's impressive comeback and Boulter's decent run creates a fascinating subplot for the leading British women in the final throes of the season - and the start of 2027.

Boulter will have the chance to further improve her ranking when she plays in Tokyo and Hong Kong in the coming weeks, with Kartal's plans for the rest of the season still uncertain as she sensibly manages her workload.

And don't forget about Emma Raducanu. It seems increasingly unlikely she will play again this season because of the shin injury which ruled her out of Wimbledon, but is clearly too good a player not to be pushing back into the top 50 when she does return.

When all three are back competing on the WTA Tour at the same time, it promises to be an interesting tussle between them in the rankings.

Boulter and Raducanu both insisted they were not transfixed by the British number one spot when they exchanged positions in 2025, instead preferring to focus on their own career paths and the bigger picture of the world rankings.

But there is no doubt that Boulter, in particular, could see the opportunity to cement her place as the nation's best player as an extra incentive to continue finishing 2026 strongly.

articles.title: Nadal: "Casi olvido que fui tenista, la vida sigue su curso"
articles.standfirst: El exdeportista español reflexiona en The Athletic acerca de su retirada con motivo de su nuevo libro 'Rafa Nadal' que narra su trayectoria a base de imágenes
articles.summary: El exdeportista español reflexiona en The Athletic acerca de su retirada con motivo de su nuevo libro 'Rafa Nadal' que narra su trayectoria a base de imágenes
articles.body: Rafa Nadal ahora lleva una nueva vida. Muy distinta a su etapa como tenista profesional. Con motivo del lanzamiento de su nuevo libro titulado 'Rafa Nadal', junto a la editorial francesa Assouline, que narra la trayectoria del campeón de 22 títulos de Grand Slam a base de fotografías inéditas, ha concedido una entrevista al medio americano 'The Athletic' (sección deportiva de 'The New York Times'). “Me retiré hace solo dos años, pero ya es como si viviera otra vida cuando jugaba al tenis”, declara Rafa. Se cumplen dos años y 13 días desde que el extenista español más laureado decidiera dar un paso al lado y colgar la raqueta con la que ha conquistado tantos éxitos. Son 92 títulos y 209 semanas como número 1 del mundo, pero afirma que: "Casi olvido que fui tenista. La vida sigue su curso”. Una mentalidad ganadora sobre la pista, y seguir hacia delante fuera de ella. Hoy, Rafa Nadal tiene otras motivaciones: "Me dedico a mis otros proyectos y a ser padre de mis hijos". Aunque también ligado al tenis de cierta forma junto a los chicos de su academia: "Trabajo en la academia, la fundación, todo esto. Trabajo y viajo mucho, más de lo que esperaba al jubilarme, y lo digo en el buen sentido”. Las lesiones han sido muy protagonistas en la carrera del manacorí. Y, aunque hayan frenado en gran parte que la carrera sea todavía más exitosa si cabe, Rafa encuentra un punto positivo: "Lo único positivo que saqué de todas las lesiones fue que pude disfrutar más y valorar más los grandes momentos". Cada trofeo significaba un éxito inigualable y un ejercicio de supervivencia: "Pero viví toda mi carrera tenística con dolor, a diario sufría demasiado". El extenista español se perdió hasta 20 Grand Slam por lesión. De las 68 ediciones que disputó, se alzó con la victoria en 22 de ellas (14 Roland Garros, 4 US Open, 2 Australian Open y 2 Wimbledon). Si hay algo que ha acompañado a Rafa Nadal durante toda su carrera, aparte de los títulos, ha sido su familia y equipo: "Pasé por todas esas dificultades, todos esos años de éxito y experiencias increíbles, momentos tristes y difíciles, pero siempre mantuve el mismo espíritu, el mismo equipo. Siempre tuve a mi familia a mi lado. Todavía conservo a los mismos amigos, desde que era pequeño. Nunca me he alejado del lugar donde nací, Mallorca. Así que, en cierto modo, he tenido muchas cosas, digamos, emotivas y exitosas, pero al mismo tiempo, mi vida real nunca cambió mucho", dejando claro que cuando el extenista volvía a casa, siempre estaba rodeado de los suyos y volvía a sentirse como el niño que creció en Manacor. El español también repasó la comparativa de estilos, a la hora de saltar a la pista, entre el propio Rafa y su gran rival y amigo, Roger Federer: "Cuando me veo con los pantalones de pirata y algunos conjuntos, pienso: vaya... qué horrible", declara en referencia a los famosos pantalones pirata con los que solía jugar el mallorquín al inicio de su carrera. "Pero al mismo tiempo, en ese momento fue algo especial, y de alguna manera también creé mi ADN con todas esas cosas, siendo un poco diferente. Siempre me ha gustado jugar con los colores". Todo esto enfrentado con la clase del suizo: "Él vestía de forma un poco más clásica. Yo era un poco más joven, él era más elegante en cuanto a su estilo de juego”.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz entrenará este sábado con Dimitrov en Viena y el domingo con Rublev
articles.standfirst: El murciano se desplaza mañana a la capital austriaca en busca de rodaje en superficie dura bajo techo
articles.summary: El murciano se desplaza mañana a la capital austriaca en busca de rodaje en superficie dura bajo techo
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ya tiene las maletas preparadas para desplazarse este sábado a Viena. El murciano será el segundo cabeza de serie del certamen de categoría 500 que sólo ha disputado en una ocasión. En 2021, alcanzó las semifinales. Alcaraz busca rodaje en superficie dura bajo techo pensando en los dos grandes objetivos hasta final de curso: las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre) y la fase final de la Copa Davis (24 al 29 de noviembre). Su bagaje en ese hábitat es de 36 triunfos por 15 derrotas, lo que da un porcentaje de efectividad del 70,06 por ciento, el más bajo que tiene de todas las superficies. Carlitos aterrizará mañana en Viena y tiene ya pista de entrenamiento en el Marx Halle, según ha podido saber MARCA, de cinco a siete de la tarde. Su 'sparring' será Grigor Dimitrov, el 123 del ranking a sus 35 años. Un día más tarde se ejercitará con el ruso Andrey Rublev, el 22 de las listas y que viene de perder en el debut de Almaty con Adrian Mannarino. El campeón de siete grandes debutará el martes 27 contra un rival que saldrá del sorteo del cuadro que se celebrará este sábado. Habrán pasado 15 días desde la derrota en la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 de Shanghái ante Zizou Bergs. Alcaraz aspira, por segundo año seguido, a llevarse el mayor botín de los torneos 500, que es el bonus a tenista que obtiene más puntos en los eventos de la categoría. El fenómeno de El Palmar, campeón en Doha y Tokio, es ahora mismo cuarto en la clasificación de 2026, con un total de 1.050 puntos. Por delante de él están Alex de Miñaur (1.280), Ben Shelton (1.250) y Taylor Fritz (1.160). De Miñaur, al igual que el murciano, está apuntado en la capital austriaca mientras que Shelton y Fritz aparecen en la lista de inscritos de la localidad helvética. La bolsa en premios que destina la ATP para los 16 mejores en los eventos 500 es de 3.070.000 dólares. El que acabe primero se llevará aproximadamente un millón de dólares, 512.500 el segundo, y 256.250 el tercero.

articles.title: Gaël Monfils defends Elina Svitolina after ‘venomous’ response to divorce announcement
articles.summary: Gaël Monfils has spoken publicly about his divorce from fellow tennis star Elina Svitolina for the first time, labeling the response to Svitolina’s announcin...
articles.body:
Gaël Monfils has spoken publicly about his divorce from fellow tennis star Elina Svitolina for the first time, labeling the response to Svitolina's announcing of their separation as "unkind at best, and venomous at worst."

Monfils, 40, who retired from tennis earlier than planned as a result of their separation, issued a statement on Instagram Friday, four days after Svitolina, 32, announced the end of their marriage, which she initially attributed to the psychological impact of Russia's invasion of her native Ukraine.

"Even though she did not owe anyone an explanation, Elina chose to speak vulnerably and truthfully about her reasons for this decision. She did so in the best way she knew how," Monfils wrote.

"Many decided that her explanation wasn't perfect enough, and Elina has now faced a kind of criticism that I have found unkind at best, and venomous at worst."

In the original announcement Monday, Svitolina wrote that she had endured sleepless nights, doubts and a feeling of losing herself since Russia's invasion in 2022.

"Gaël saw all of it," she wrote. "He never let go of my hand. We fought through this together for a long time, with everything we had. But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you.

"With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage."

In a second statement, released Tuesday, Svitolina suggested that she had not planned to release such a public statement, but did so after Monfils' early retirement, which was confirmed last week, prompted rumors about why he had chosen to curtail his career earlier than November's Paris Masters.

The Frenchman had been scheduled to play at this week's ATP 250 event in Lyon, France, with an exhibition planned alongside countrymen Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, Richard Gasquet and Gilles Simon.

"I shared only one of the reasons that influenced my decision to reflect on my life and my future. But the truth is, there's so much more to it, and it was never just about one thing," Svitolina wrote.

The pair married in July 2021 and have a daughter, Skaï, born in October 2022. They reached the U.S. Open mixed doubles semifinals together in August, with Svitolina enjoying one of the best singles seasons of her career following a decision to end her 2025 season early due to burnout caused in part by the impact of Russia's invasion. In his statement issued Friday, Monfils wrote: "Though my heart hurts, I am forever grateful to her for her support and love over the years. When I was ready to quit tennis, she gave me the encouragement I needed to continue."

Monfils also echoed Svitolina's conviction that they remained a family, still have love for each other, and would dedicate themselves to raising their daughter.

"Elina has her battles to fight, just as I have mine. I respect her choices and reasons, and we will continue to support and care deeply about each other, especially as two people who share a child," he wrote.

"As we move through this new chapter, I would ask everyone to remember that we are all just human beings: not Gaël Monfils and Elina Svitolina, but Gaël and Elina. Imperfect, but trying our best."

articles.title: Los rivales directos de Jódar y Davidovich siguen sumando de cara a las ATP Finals
articles.standfirst: Medvedev, Fils, Tommy Paul y Fritz, presentes esta semana en Almaty, Bruselas y Lyon, amenazan a los españoles en la 'race' del torneo de maestros
articles.summary: Medvedev, Fils, Tommy Paul y Fritz, presentes esta semana en Almaty, Bruselas y Lyon, amenazan a los españoles en la 'race' del torneo de maestros
articles.body: Son 23 días los que restan para las Nitto ATP Finals (15 al 22 de noviembre) y solo tienen asegurado su puesto tres jugadores: Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz y Ben Shelton. Hasta 12 jugadores se están jugando su plaza en Turín. Desde el quinto puesto, marcado actualmente por Flavio Cobolli, separan 1.190 puntos con el decimosexto, ocupado por Alejandro Davidovich. Además de los ATP 250 de Almaty, Bruselas, Lyon y Estocolmo, todavía faltan por disputarse los 500 de Viena y Basilea (donde están presentes Jódar y Davidovich) y la gran cita del Masters 1000 de París (2 al 8 de noviembre). El ruso, actualmente sexto en la carrera, ha derrotado por doble 6-4 al francés Terence Atmane para avanzar a la ronda de los cuatro mejores. Daniil suma 3.520 puntos, 361 más que Rafa Jódar. Medvedev es el encargado de defender el título en tierras kazajas. Se llevó la edición de 2025 ante el francés Corentin Moutet. Le espera el local Alexander Bublik en la que será su 73ª aparición en unas semifinales ATP. El francés, que se había presentado en los cuartos de final del torneo belga sin jugar (tras la retirada de Munar), ha superado al americano Alex Michelsen por 6-4 y 7-6 (12). Fils cuenta con 3.425 puntos en su haber. Octavo en la 'race', es el que precede al madrileño en la tabla. Tan solo les separan 261 puntos. Tendrá en frente al ganador del duelo entre Zizou Bergs y Jan-Lennard Struff por un puesto en la final. Los americanos también se han plantado en la penúltima ronda del torneo francés. Tommy Paul superó primero a Moutet por 6-4, 3-6 y 6-3, para después hacer lo mismo su compañero de medalla olímpica, Taylor Fritz, ante el alemán Daniel Altmaier por 7-6 (5) y 6-2. Estos amenazan más a Alejandro Davidovich en la posibilidad de asalto a su primera copa de maestros, ya que que ambos están por encima del español. Tommy Paul cuenta con 2.685 puntos, 235 más que el reciente campeón del Masters 1000 de Shanghái, mientras que la distancia con Taylor Fritz se reduce a 180 puntos. La próxima semana dará comienzo el ATP 500 de Basilea. Además de presenciar la retirada de Stan Wawrinka; Rafa Jódar y Alejandro Davidovich lucharán por seguir aumentando sus posibilidades por entrar entre los ocho mejores del año. Jódar es el que está, a día de hoy, virtualmente clasificado. Su noveno puesto lo confirma momentáneamente. Aunque no estarán solos en la lucha. En Basilea se suma otro factor más, la presencia de Novak Djokovic. El serbio, que aceptó la invitación del certamen suizo, ocupa el decimoprimer puesto de la carrera a Turín con 2.840 puntos. También vive una situación límite en términos clasificatorios, ya que se encuentra a 319 puntos del madrileño, que marca el corte.

articles.title: Gael Monfils condemns criticism of Elina Svitolina after pair's separation following five years of marriage
articles.summary: Elina Svitolina announced her and Gael Monfils' separation earlier in the week; addressing the split in an Instagram post on Friday,  Monfils labelled some of the criticism of Svitolina as "venomous"; the pair married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter
articles.body:
Svitolina announced the end of one of tennis' most high-profile relationships in an emotional post on Instagram earlier this week, where she attributed the split in part to the mental toll of Russia's ongoing war in her native Ukraine.

That promoted a wave of hostility online towards the world No 6, which increased when she then confirmed that the end of the marriage had led Monfils to retire earlier than planned.

The 40-year-old Frenchman had been due to bow out at the Paris Masters next month but his second-round loss to Learner Tien at the US Open ended up being his last as a professional.

Monfils leapt to the defence of Svitolina in an Instagram post on Friday, saying: "Even though she did not owe anyone an explanation, Elina chose to speak vulnerably and truthfully about her reasons for this decision.

"She did so in the best way she knew how. Many decided that her explanation wasn't perfect enough and Elina has now faced a kind of criticism that I have found unkind at best and venomous at worst.

"Elina and I may no longer be a couple, but we are still a family. Though my heart hurts, I am forever grateful to her for her support and love over the years.

"While I am deeply grateful that the public feels so invested in my happiness, I have found the lack of grace and kindness shown towards Elina upsetting.

"While some may not understand her reasons, or agree with them, please remember that there is so much more that happens in a relationship behind the curtain that cannot be explained in a post.

"Elina has her battles to fight, just as I have mine. I respect her choices and reasons, and we will continue to support and care deeply about each other, especially as two people who share a child."

Svitolina - a four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist - and former world No 6 Monfils married in 2021 and have a four-year-old daughter called Skai.

In her social media post announcing their separation, Svitolina said she had come to realise she needed to rediscover herself and could no longer do so within her marriage.

"This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote.

"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside.

"With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.

"It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love. Gael listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget."

She added: "Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not.

"Please know that there is no one to blame here. There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape."

Only a few months ago Svitolina and Monfils had joined forces to reach the semi-finals of the US Open Mixed Doubles Championship.

Svitolina and Monfils had impressed in the tournament until coming up against Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the last four.

More recently, Svitolina was in action at the Wuhan Open, but ran into an inspired Sonay Kartal, with the Brit winning their quarter-final clash in three sets.

articles.title: What the WTA Finals looked like the last time Serena Williams won the event in 2014
articles.summary: The WTA Finals are a hugely prestigious end-of-year event, where the eight best players that year give it all they’ve got for one final chance...
articles.body:
The WTA Finals are a hugely prestigious end-of-year event, where the eight best players that year give it all they've got for one final chance at glory.

There are no free places on offer in an event like this, with every player forced to earn their spots through consistent performances across a ten-month period.

Their reward is the opportunity to face the world's best in a unique format, with huge money and ranking points on offer.

Although some way behind, Serena Williams is joined by Steffi Graf on five, having won her final one in 2014.

When Serena Williams made history at the 2014 WTA Finals

2014 was an outstanding year for Williams, who won the most titles (seven), accrued the most points (8,487), and justifiably topped the Race to the WTA Finals leaderboard.

Maria Sharapova was not far behind though, with Petra Kvitova and Simona Halep making up the rest of the top four.

Beyond this quartet, there was a group of hugely talented players with far fewer points, as Eugenie Bouchard, Agnieszka Radwańska, Ana Ivanovic and Caroline Wozniacki rounded out the eight participants.

Interestingly, Li Na actually won the Australian Open that year, but this was a good decade before the WTA implemented the rule that allowed anyone who had won a major that year to bypass the traditional top-eight qualification process. The Chinese star finished ninth in the race.

Williams would go on to win that year's WTA Finals, comfortably beating Halep in the final by a 6-3, 6-3 margin.

This compounded a stellar end to the 2014 season, where the American had also claimed the US Open title.

Who has qualified for this year's WTA Finals?

The eight participants in this year's WTA Finals have already been set, and it promises a hugely competitive affair where it really feels like anybody could win.

Elena Rybakina, who won both the Australian and US Open, naturally secured qualification with ease. Aryna Sabalenka, who lost in both finals of these events, is behind by some distance.

Mirra Andreeva won her maiden Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, and will compete in her first WTA Finals this year with Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff and Elina Svitolina all also confirmed.

Linda Noskova may be eighth in the race, but winning Wimbledon secured her spot.

This meant Karolina Muchova, her fellow Czech and Wimbledon finalist, snatched the final spot ahead of the likes of Iga Swiatek, Marta Kostyuk and Iva Jovic.

articles.title: The advice Andy Murray gave Nick Kyrgios in 2016 to try and help him reach his full potential
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios is perhaps one of the biggest ‘what ifs’ in tennis over the past 15 years. The Australian showed remarkable promise when he burst...
articles.body:
Nick Kyrgios is perhaps one of the biggest 'what ifs' in tennis over the past 15 years.

The Australian showed remarkable promise when he burst onto the scene at the 2014 Wimbledon Championships, beating Rafael Nadal en route to his first Grand Slam quarterfinal. Kyrgios has gone on to clinch seven tour-level titles and reach the final of Wimbledon in 2022.

His career has, by no means, been a failure, but many feel it is a far cry from what his potential suggested. Kyrgios, now 31 years of age, has received advice from several tennis greats over the years, including Andy Murray , who gave his opinion after beating him at the All England Club in 2016.

What Andy Murray said about Nick Kyrgios in 2016

Following a straight sets loss to Murray in the fourth round of Wimbledon that year, Kyrgios described his performance as 'pathetic'. Asked if Kyrgios needs to work on staying present all the way throughout matches, the Scot replied: "Yeah, of course he does, yeah. Yeah, of course."

He expanded: "I mean, everyone's different. It's about, you know, finding the right people to help you with different things. For some it may be a coach. For some it might be a psychologist. Sometimes it might be speaking to family about stuff.

"You know, there's not one way of tackling it. But if you want to continue to get better, then you speak and listen to, you know, as many people as you can, and take on board the things you think will help you. But everyone's different in terms of how they, you know, improve and address their problems."

Murray continued: "Just keep your head down really. Concentrate on your side of the court. Control what you can, basically. You know, you can't always control what your opponent's doing or how your opponent's playing. But you can apply yourself, you know, to every single point and fight for every point.

"You know, don't give up any cheap games or anything like that. I did a good job of that today. I don't think I gave up a breakpoint. I was solid on my serve. Then, you know, created a little chance end of the first set. After that, you know, in the second set especially, I just tried to make as many balls as possible. That was it," concluded Murray, who won the match 7-5, 6-1, 6-4.

Andy Murray said it wasn't easy finding the right team in tennis

Asked how hard it was for him to find the right team to have around him to guide him to Grand Slam glory, Murray replied: "Yeah, it's not easy. I think for tennis players, as well, especially it's hard because you're responsible for the team that's around you.

"In a way, you're in charge because you're the one that's funding it, paying it. Sometimes some people might be telling you what they think they want you to hear rather than what you really need to hear. When you're young, it isn't that easy to make those decisions.

"Sometimes if you don't think someone on your team is doing something right, when you're 19, 20 years old, to tell someone who is 40, Actually, you know, I think you could be pushing me, I don't like it when you do this, that takes time to learn how to do that. You know, it's not easy.

"But over the years, yeah, you start to know what it is you need and what you want. A lot of the guys on my team have been around me for a very long time. Obviously the more stability, the better. Coaches do change sometimes because it's a lot of travel, it's a lot of work. Not everyone's willing to put in that work."

After their match at Wimbledon in 2016, Kyrgios and Murray played two more times. Kyrgios beat Murray for the first time in 2018 at Queen's, but the Briton won their last meeting in Stuttgart in 2022.

articles.title: Bolinhas de tênis: fábrica de Jundiaí produz para torneios mundiais | G1
articles.standfirst: Há 40 anos, fábrica do interior de SP produz e exporta bolinhas de tênis para marcas esportivas ao redor do mundo. A produção mistura etapas com maquinário industrial e finalização artesanal.
articles.summary: Há 40 anos, a fábrica de bolinhas de tênis em Jundiaí produz 30 mil unidades mensais que equipam grandes marcas e torneios internacionais do esporte.
articles.body:
🎾 Por mês, mais de 30 mil bolinhas de tênis são produzidas em Jundiaí (SP) e exportadas para o mundo. A fábrica responsável por este trabalho se divide entre a linha de produção com máquinas e o toque artesanal para garantir a qualidade do "quique" perfeito que ela deve entregar.

As bolinhas que saem de Jundiaí são encomendadas por outras marcas esportivas que patrocinam os principais campeonatos do esporte fora do país. É por isso que é possível afirmar que, nas disputas entre os melhores tenistas do mundo, uma produção do interior de SP provavelmente fez parte do espetáculo, indo de um lado da quadra para outro.

José Osvaldo Osti iniciou a fábrica há 40 anos, quando juntou sua formação profissional em engenharia com sua paixão esportiva: o tênis. "Eu conheci um químico e ele cedeu pra mim um livro, onde tinha uma pequena fórmula de como fazer uma bolinha de tênis. Eu parti daí", explica.

Fábrica de Jundiaí produz bolinhas de tênis há 40 anos — Foto: TV TEM / Reprodução

O engenheiro químico Murilo Osti destaca os resultados que a fábrica da família já alcançou ao longo dos anos. "Nós tivemos uma bola de beach tennis homologada pela ITF, que é a Federação Internacional de Tênis, e para nós isso é uma alegria... Ter a nossa bola rodando na mão dos grandes jogadores e nos grandes torneios"

As etapas de produção de uma bolinha de tênis passam pela modelagem da borracha, a aplicação da capa de feltro e o mais importante: o teste da capacidade da bolinha em quicar até 1,51m.

Antes de chegar no produto final, a produção se inicia com uma mistura exata de 25 compostos químicos, que garantem a pressão perfeita que irá envolver a borracha. Após o molde de uma meia-esfera, elas seguem para uma prensa de alta temperatura e depois são lixadas, até que cheguem na fase da colagem das duas metades que completam uma bolinha.

Depois de todo o processo químico e de formação, entra em cena o feltro de lã, que irá envolver a bolinha e dar a sua característica de cor. Em Jundiaí, ele é cortado e colado manualmente, antes de ir para o forno final.

Fábrica de Jundiaí produz bolinhas de tênis há mais de 40 anos — Foto: TV TEM / Reprodução

Por fim, depois de mais de 12 horas de produção, a bolinha vai para o teste final de qualidade. Ao ser lançada a uma altura de 2,54 metros, ela tem que quicar e chegar à altura de, no mínimo, 1,38m ou, no máximo, 1,51m.

articles.title: 'Venomous at worst': Gael Monfils breaks silence on separation from Elina Svitolina
articles.summary: Gael Monfils has spoken publicly about his separation from Elina Svitolina, defending the Ukrainian tennis star after she faced heavy criticism over the
articles.body: Gael Monfils has spoken publicly about his separation from Elina Svitolina, defending the Ukrainian tennis star after she faced heavy criticism over the end of their five-year marriage.The French player expressed his disappointment with the negative reactions and urged fans to respect their private lives instead of blaming Svitolina for his early retirement.In an emotional Instagram statement shared Friday, Monfils thanked Svitolina for supporting him throughout his career and criticized the harsh comments directed at her."Many decided that her explanation wasn't perfect enough, and Elina has now faced a kind of criticism that I have found unkind at best, and venomous at worst," Monfils wrote.The statement came four days after Svitolina announced their separation, explaining that the emotional strain of Russia's war in Ukraine and other personal challenges had affected her deeply.Retirement reports fuel criticismAccording to French sports newspaper L'Équipe, Svitolina reportedly told Monfils during a phone call in late September that she wanted to end their marriage. Monfils was in Dubai with their daughter, Skai, while Svitolina was competing in Beijing.Reports suggested that the conversation deeply affected Monfils, who later withdrew from his remaining tournaments. He had planned to end his 22-year professional career at the Paris Masters in November, but instead announced his retirement, effective October 5.His final professional singles match was his second-round defeat to Learner Tien at the US Open. Monfils finished his career with 13 ATP titles and reached two Grand Slam semifinals.As details of his retirement emerged, some fans blamed Svitolina for disrupting his planned farewell, while others questioned her reasons for ending the marriage. Several argued that she should have waited until after the Paris Masters to make the decision.Monfils stresses family comes firstThe backlash also drew criticism from former Australian player and coach Rennae Stubbs, who reminded fans that outsiders cannot fully understand what happens within a marriage.Monfils shared a similar view, expressing his frustration with the treatment of his estranged wife. "While I am deeply grateful that the public feels so invested in my happiness, I have found the lack of grace and kindness shown towards Elina upsetting," he wrote.Despite their separation, Monfils made it clear that he continues to respect and care for Svitolina. The couple married in July 2021 and welcomed their daughter in October 2022."Elina and I may no longer be a couple, but we are still a family," he wrote, emphasizing that their daughter remains their priority.He also acknowledged the personal struggles both are facing, adding, "Elina has her battles to fight just as I have mine."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Monfils defiende a Svitolina tras su separación: "Estoy conmocionado por la falta de amabilidad hacia ella"
articles.standfirst: El francés responde a los ataques recibidos por la ucraniana tras anunciar su ruptura y pide respeto para afrontar un proceso que afecta a toda la familia
articles.summary: El francés responde a los ataques recibidos por la ucraniana tras anunciar su ruptura y pide respeto para afrontar un proceso que afecta a toda la familia
articles.body: Gael Monfils ha salido en defensa de Elina Svitolina. Tras el anuncio de su separación y las críticas que ha recibido la tenista ucraniana en las redes sociales, el francés ha publicado un extenso mensaje en Instagram para pedir respeto hacia quien ha compartido su vida. "Elina y yo puede que ya no seamos una pareja, pero seguimos siendo una familia", escribe en una publicación acompañada por un primer plano de ella. La ruptura de una de las parejas más conocidas del circuito ha tenido una exposición que Monfils ha querido frenar. Svitolina explicó públicamente su decisión y recibió una oleada de comentarios que el francés considera injustos. "Aunque no tenía que dar explicaciones a nadie, Elina eligió hablar de forma vulnerable y sincera sobre sus razones para tomar esta decisión. Lo hizo de la mejor manera que sabía. Muchos decidieron que su explicación no era adecuada, y Elina se enfrentó a una serie de críticas que encontré, en el mejor de los casos, descorteses y, en el peor, venenosas". Ambos habían acostumbrado a sus seguidores a compartir alegrías y momentos difíciles. Esa cercanía les convirtió en una pareja muy seguida, también fuera de las pistas. Ahora atraviesan una situación cuyo alcance no cabe en una publicación. "Como sabe cualquiera que haya vivido el final de una relación, no es algo fácil de afrontar. Una separación es un campo de minas de sentimientos caóticos y complicados por el que Elina y yo estamos intentando avanzar lo mejor posible", explica Monfils. El francés sitúa el respeto mutuo en el centro de ese proceso. "Y lo estamos haciendo con el gran respeto y el amor que todavía sentimos, y siempre sentiremos, el uno por el otro. Estoy conmocionado por la falta de amabilidad mostrada hacia ella. Por favor, recordad que en una relación suceden muchas cosas entre bastidores que no pueden explicarse en una publicación". Svitolina afronta, además, el sufrimiento provocado por la guerra en su país, una circunstancia que forma parte del difícil momento personal de la ucraniana. La información publicada por La Gazzetta dello Sport vincula también la separación con la decisión de Monfils de adelantar su retirada de la competición, una despedida que se produjo casi en silencio. En su mensaje, el exnúmero seis del mundo recuerda precisamente el apoyo que recibió de Svitolina cuando se planteó dejar el tenis. "Aunque ahora me duela el corazón, siempre le estaré agradecido por su apoyo y su amor a lo largo de los años. Cuando estaba preparado para dejar de jugar al tenis, ella me dio el ánimo que necesitaba para continuar". Entre esos recuerdos aparece su hija Skai, a la que Monfils dedica una de las frases más personales del mensaje. "Ella es la persona que está detrás de algunas de las victorias más grandes de mi vida: como nuestra hija Skai, que es la mayor de todas". La pequeña seguirá uniendo a los dos tenistas en esta nueva etapa, para la que el francés reclama comprensión y espacio. La publicación termina con una petición dirigida a quienes opinan sobre su separación: "Pediría a todos que recordaran que solo somos seres humanos. No Gael Monfils y Elina Svitolina, sino Gael y Elina. Imperfectos, que hacen lo mejor que pueden".

articles.title: Japan Open: Katie Boulter loses to Katerina Siniakova in semi-finals
articles.summary: New British number one Katie Boulter loses 6-1 6-4 to Czech doubles specialist Katerina Siniakova in the Japan Open semi-finals.
articles.body:
Katie Boulter has lost in the Japan Open semi-finals, in her first match since reclaiming the British number one spot from Sonny Kartal.

Kartal moved above Boulter in the world rankings by reaching the final of last week's Wuhan Open.

But Boulter's run to the last four in Osaka, which included a victory over Antonia Ruzic in the quarter-finals, will be enough for her to go back above Kartal when the rankings are next updated.

However, the 30-year-old missed the chance to reach the final, and a shot at a fifth WTA singles title, losing 6-1 6-4 to doubles world number one Siniakova.

Eighth seed Boulter rallied after being swept aside in the opening set, going a break up at the start of the second.

But Siniakova, also 30, maintained her bid for a first singles title in four years by claiming two hard-fought breaks of her own to wrap up victory in 85 minutes.

She will now play 2023 champion Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final after the 22-year-old American beat compatriot and top seed Ann Li 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-3.

The Czech won the first five games of the match and Boulter had to save a set point to win her first game.

Boulter stirred hopes of a fightback when she broke Siniakova but her opponent soon seized back control.

The Briton showed greater resistance in the second set but Siniakova served out for a straightforward victory.

Siniakova, the world No 86, will face USA's Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final.

The world No 55 beat fellow American Ann Li in Saturday's other semi-final, knocking out the No 1 seed in three sets.

articles.title: Rybakina readies for title defence at Ningbo Open in final with Fernandez
articles.summary: The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova.
articles.body:
Defending Ningbo Open champion Elena Rybakina overcame Russian sixth seed Diana Shnaider 6-3, 7-5 in the semifinal to reach another title clash and remind rivals of her threat before next month’s WTA Finals.

The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final on Sunday after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova by the same 6-3, 7-5 scoreline in the earlier semifinal at the Yinzhou International Tennis Centre in the eastern Chinese city.

Australian and US Open champion Rybakina, who arrived for her title defence after a bruising defeat in Beijing and a foot injury that forced her out of Wuhan, showed flashes of her best form despite a few wobbles against the 13th-ranked Shnaider.

“She [Shnaider] played really well, and it’s always difficult to play against left-handers. We don’t have so many on the tour,” said Rybakina, who faces a similar test against Fernandez.

“I needed some time. The returns were not as bad, but during the rallies, to switch the pattern was a little bit of an issue for me, but I’m happy I managed to win in two sets.”

An aggressive start with powerful winners from deep helped three-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina take full control of the opening frame, which she sealed on her 11th set point after a sudden dip in form.

“It was an important game, and it was a long one,” added the top-seeded Rybakina.

“It was on my serve, and it was a struggle … I was playing the first balls really well, but I couldn’t close the game … so many opportunities, but I’m glad it went my way. She played some great shots and great rallies.”

The 27-year-old continued to struggle with the accuracy of her first serve in the next set, but won the crucial points and carved out a 4-3 advantage with a break, only to be broken to love in the 10th game.

Rybakina responded strongly to get her nose in front again in the next game with some big hitting, before closing out the victory with a much more assured display on serve to take her place in the final.

She will aim to further sharpen her game in Sunday’s final before turning her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week and then launching her WTA Finals title defence at Indian Wells from November 8.

“It’s never easy,” Rybakina said about winning back-to-back trophies at the Ningbo Open. “Of course I’ll try to do my best. I’m going to fight and give my all tomorrow.”

articles.summary: El malagueño se estrenará ante Bergs mientras que el madrileño jugará su primer partido con Tabilo

El madrileño es noveno de la Race 2026, con una renta de 649 puntos respecto a su compatriota. Basilea pone en juego una bolsa de 500 puntos para el campeón y habrá otros 1.000 en el Masters 1000 de París. En la pelea por la cita de maestros están también Arthur Fils (7), Novak Djokovic (11) y Taylor Fritz (12), los tres presentes en tierras helvéticas. Djokovic aceptó una invitación de la organización para apurar sus opciones de clasificación a Turín, un evento al que renunció las dos últimas temporadas y en el que tiene el récord de siete títulos. Nole debutará con el galo Ugo Humbert. El momento más emotivo se vivirá en Basilea con Stan Wawrinka. El tenista local cuelga oficialmente la raqueta a sus 41 años. articles.title: Gael Monfils defends Elina Svitolina from 'venomous' criticism
articles.summary: Gael Monfils describes criticism of Elina Svitolina since she announced the pair were ending their marriage as "venomous" and "upsetting".
articles.body:
Gael Monfils has described criticism of Elina Svitolina since she announced the pair were ending their marriage as "venomous" and "upsetting".

Svitolina cited the emotional impact of the war in her native Ukraine, which was invaded by Russia in February 2022, as part of the reason for the split with Frenchman Monfils.

The couple married in 2021 and have one child together - a four-year-old daughter called Skai.

"Even though she did not owe anyone an explanation, Elina chose to speak vulnerably and truthfully about her reasons for this decision," wrote Monfils in a social media post. , external

"She did so in the best way she knew how. Many decided that her explanation wasn't perfect enough and Elina has now faced a kind of criticism that I have found unkind at best and venomous at worst.

"Elina and I may no longer be a couple, but we are still a family. Though my heart hurts, I am forever grateful to her for her support and love over the years.

"While I am deeply grateful that the public feels so invested in my happiness, I have found the lack of grace and kindness shown towards Elina upsetting.

"While some may not understand her reasons, or agree with them, please remember that there is so much more that happens in a relationship behind the curtain that cannot be explained in a post.

"Elina has her battles to fight, just as I have mine. I respect her choices and reasons, and we will continue to support and care deeply about each other, especially as two people who share a child."

articles.title: Ons Jabeur trained on temporary hotel courts in Tunisia before reaching Grand Slam finals: How family sacrifices, determination and an unconventional tennis journey helped her inspire a generation of Arab women athletes
articles.summary: Discover the remarkable story of Ons Jabeur, the first Arab woman to reach Grand Slam finals, whose journey from makeshift hotel courts in Tunisia to the world stage is a testament to family sacrifices and determination.
articles.body: Ons Jabeur’s ascent in professional tennis started far from the game’s most hallowed academies. She grew up in Tunisia, where she had less access to tennis courts and had to make do with what she could find, including temporary hotel courts. Her early journey was one of patience, consistent practice and a willingness to keep trying in a sport where opportunities didn’t always come easily.There was a family behind that ambition, a family willing to make great sacrifices. Supported by her parents and siblings, Jabeur was able to continue developing her game, and her creativity and determination helped her to develop a style that stood apart. She became a trailblazer for Arab and African women in tennis with her later Grand Slam finals appearances.How family sacrifices shaped Ons Jabeur’s tennis careerJabeur’s early development depended on more than natural talent. Her mother, Samira, introduced her to tennis when she was a young child, taking her to courts at hotels in Hammam Sousse. With dedicated tennis facilities limited in her surroundings, these spaces became an important starting point for a player who would eventually compete against the world’s best.Her family also helped her access more specialised coaching. Training sometimes meant travelling considerable distances, requiring time, planning and financial commitment, and these efforts helped Jabeur build the foundations of her game before she moved to Tunis as a teenager to pursue more structured training.How Ons Jabeur rose from Tunisia’s hotel courtsIt took years of development and adaptation to get Jabeur from the hotel courts to the international stage. As a junior, she would sometimes play against boys, gaining experience in an environment where opportunities for girls weren’t so advanced, and those early experiences helped her forge a competitive game founded on movement, touch and tactical awareness.She moved to Tunis at 12 to get access to more specialised tennis training. That move was a major step toward a professional career and a more structured sporting environment, and it wasn’t without its challenges: Players from countries with fewer established pathways to the professional game can struggle to find sponsorship, consistent competition and the same visibility as athletes from traditional tennis powerhouses.But Jabeur’s style was unique and not just all about power, with her use of drop shots, slices, change of pace and surprise angles making her hard to read. The variety became an asset, allowing her to face opponents used to more predictable baseline skirmishes.How Ons Jabeur inspired a new generation of tennis playersJabeur’s influence extends beyond rankings and tournament results. Her success has given young athletes across Tunisia, North Africa and the wider Arab world a prominent example of someone who reached the highest levels of tennis without beginning in one of the sport’s traditional centres. Her journey has helped challenge assumptions about where elite players can emerge.Ultimately, her story is not simply about reaching Grand Slam finals. It is about the family support that helped sustain an early dream, the determination required to overcome barriers and the confidence to preserve an individual playing identity. From temporary hotel courts in Tunisia to the biggest stages in tennis, Ons Jabeur has shown a generation of aspiring athletes that the route to the top does not have to begin in a traditional tennis powerhouse.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Naomi Osaka 'not far off' her best but ponders long-term future
articles.summary: Four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka says she is returning to her best form but would consider quitting the game if asked to by her three-year-old daughter.
articles.body:
Naomi Osaka says she is "not far off" the form that saw her win four Grand Slam titles, but admits she has thought about quitting and often ponders her future.

The 29-year-old Japanese star twice won both the US Open and Australian Open, between 2018 and 2021, during a glittering start to her career that saw her rise to number one in the world.

But she took time out of the sport in 2021 to prioritise her mental health and another 15 months away after becoming pregnant, before returning in 2023 following the birth of her daughter.

Osaka now says that she would quit tennis if her three-year-old, Shai, asked her to, despite climbing back up the world rankings and once again challenging for major titles.

"It's tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I'm going to play," said Osaka, as she prepares to take part in the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.

"Because if my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that."

'I'm very proud of myself' - Osaka wins on comeback

Osaka withdraws from French Open Published 31 May 2021

Osaka beats Brady to win Australian Open Published 20 February 2021

Osaka beats Brady to win Australian Open

Osaka acknowledged that her mindset has changed a lot with age and the extra responsibilities that come with parenthood, saying "my daughter is my biggest priority".

"I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis," she added.

"I wouldn't say I'm part-timing it but my entire day doesn't consist of that.

"If I think about it in certain ways, I'm really proud of where I am now because it's not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport."

Osaka has battled her way back up to 19th in the world and is the seventh seed at this week's tournament, where she plays Italy's Jasmine Paolini in the opening round.

She beat top seed Aryna Sabalenka on her way to the quarter-finals of Wimbledon earlier this year, after finishing runner-up in the preceding grass tournament at Bad Homburg, and also reached the last 16 of the French Open and US Open.

Osaka also made it to the semi-finals in Washington and last eight in Toronto during the North American hardcourt swing, and her run at Flushing Meadows was only ended by eventual champion Elena Rybakina.

"I genuinely don't feel like I'm that far off," she said, when considering if she can get back to winning titles.

"I think there are certain instincts that I don't want to say I lost, but maybe I forgot and I'm kind of relearning but yeah, I don't think - I hope - I'm not far off.

"I think I built a pretty solid base and I'm just excited to see if I can continue learning and going further in tournaments."

Osaka is in the opposite side of the draw in Tokyo to Kazakhstan's world number one Rybakina, who goes into the tournament on the back of winning her fourth title of the year at the Ningbo Open in China.

The defending champion powered past Canada's Leylah Fernandez 6-2 6-2 in Sunday's final to claim a first tournament victory since last month's US Open.

articles.title: Rybakina beats Fernandez to defend Ningbo Open title and claim 1st title since earning No. 1 ranking
articles.summary: NINGBO, China (AP) — Elena Rybakina claimed her first trophy since earning the No. 1 ranking, beating Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 on Sunday to defend her Ningb...
articles.body:
NINGBO, China (AP) — Elena Rybakina claimed her first trophy since earning the No. 1 ranking , beating Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 on Sunday to defend her Ningbo Open title.

Rybakina moved past Aryna Sabalenka into the top spot after the U.S. Open but was then stunned by 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva in her opening match at the China Open.

It's Rybakina's tour-leading fourth title of the year to go with her Australian Open, Stuttgart and U.S. Open trophies; and the 15th of her career.

Rybakina improved to 8-0 in her career at the Ningbo Open after beating Ekaterina Alexandrova in last season's final.

Against the 30th-ranked Fernandez, a U.S. Open finalist in 2021, Rybakina saved all four break points she faced and produced a forehand winner on her first match point.

articles.title: Rybakina gana en Ningbo su primer título como Nº1
articles.standfirst: La kazaja cerró la final en 77 minutos ante Leylah Fernández y defiende un certamen por primera vez en su carrera
articles.summary: La kazaja cerró la final en 77 minutos ante Leylah Fernández y defiende un certamen por primera vez en su carrera
articles.body: Elena Rybakina ya tiene su primer título como nueva reina del circuito WTA. Lo ha conseguido en la final de Ningbo ante la canadiense Leylah Fernández por doble 6-2. Es el cuarto certamen que levanta en 2026, tras los grandes en Australia y Nueva York, y el 500 sobre la tierra de Stuttgart. En 77 minutos, el público del Centro Yinzhou de Tenis de Ningbo vio como Rybakina le endosaba un contundente correctivo a la que una vez fuera finalista del US Open 2021. Una ventisca de 24 golpes ganadores (por 10 de la canadiense) fue lo que dictaminó que la kazaja levantara su decimoquinto título y celebrara la victoria número 53 de la temporada en 20 torneos disputados. Es la primera vez en la carrera de la actual número 1 del mundo que defiende un certamen, ya que también se hizo con el WTA chino en 2025. El ruso Daniil Medvedev también podría cumplir esta hazaña si levanta hoy el título en Almaty ante el georgiano Nikoloz Basilashvili.
